identity.operation: Release a parsed document through XMLNode descendant cleanup.
identity.condition: The parsed document has child nodes and is destroyed or cleared.
identity.capability: XMLNode must safely delete descendants through the relevant DeleteChildren/DeleteChild or DeleteNode path.
identity.consequence: Descendant cleanup may fail during document release.

requirement: Releasing a parsed document with child nodes must safely delete its descendants.

assessment.necessity_reason: The old harness parses into a local XMLDocument, and g0001 changes how an XMLNode destructor deletes children. The supplied evidence does not establish a cleanup failure or confirm safe cleanup on either side.

before.requirement: Releasing a parsed document with child nodes must safely delete its descendants.
before.reason: The old XMLNode destructor calls DeleteChildren, which delegates to DeleteChild. The supplied evidence omits DeleteChild and the document destruction path.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: DeleteChildren delegates each child deletion to DeleteChild.
The harness's Parse call can invoke child cleanup after a parse error.

after.requirement: Releasing a parsed document with child nodes must safely delete its descendants.
after.reason: The changed XMLNode destructor clears each child's parent and calls DeleteNode. The implementation of that XMLNode deletion function and the document destruction path are not supplied.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The harness's Parse call retains a child-cleanup path after a parse error.

assessment.comparison_reason: The same local-document cleanup requirement applies before and after g0001. No concrete old-harness blocker or confirmed cleanup outcome is established on either side.
missing_information: XMLDocument::~XMLDocument is needed to trace release of the local document.
XMLNode::DeleteChild, XMLNode::DeleteNode, and XMLNode::Unlink are needed to assess the deletion paths.
XMLNode::ParseDeep is needed to establish how parsed child nodes enter the cleanup path.

necessity_evidence.reason: The old harness parses into a local XMLDocument, and g0001 changes XMLNode descendant cleanup. The supplied packet establishes the cleanup obligation but neither a failure nor safe completion of that cleanup.

scope_contract.reason: The entry parses into a local document, so releasing its parsed descendants is part of its lifecycle.

feasible_trigger.reason: The entry can supply XML text to Parse, which calls ParseDeep, but the supplied code does not trace a child-bearing parsed tree through destruction.

evidence.dependency_reason: Parse delegates tree construction to ParseDeep.

observable_consequence.reason: The new destructor calls XMLNode::DeleteNode for each child, but its implementation and the document destruction path are not supplied. No cleanup failure is established.

evidence.dependency_reason: The local document's lifetime ends when the entry returns.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: The supplied XMLDocument::DeleteNode body calls XMLNode::DeleteNode; it does not show what the destructor's XMLNode::DeleteNode call does. The old DeleteChildren path likewise delegates to an unsupplied DeleteChild body.

evidence.dependency_reason: This is XMLDocument::DeleteNode, which delegates to the distinct XMLNode::DeleteNode function.
The old cleanup path delegates to DeleteChild.

identity_preserved.reason: Both versions are assessed against the same obligation: safe descendant cleanup when the old entry's parsed local document is released.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Shows the old destructor's delegated child cleanup.
Distinguishes XMLDocument::DeleteNode from the unsupplied XMLNode::DeleteNode body.

missing_information: The document destruction and parsed-child construction paths are needed to establish a finite child-bearing cleanup execution.
The deletion implementations are needed to determine whether either cleanup path fails.
